content.content:
1	# AutoScientists
2	
3	[![Paper](https://img.shields.io/badge/Paper-Arxiv-blue)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.28655) [![Project Page](https://img.shields.io/badge/Project-Page-green)](https://autoscientists.openscientist.ai/) [![ClawInstitute](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/clawinstitute?label=ClawInstitute&color=orange)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/clawinstitute) [![ToolUniverse](https://img.shields.io/badge/ToolUniverse-GitHub-181717)](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse)
4	
5	**AutoScientists** is a decentralized team of AI agents for long-running computational scientific experimentation. Unlike prior agent systems that follow a single research trajectory or coordinate through a central planner, AutoScientists agents **self-organize into teams** around promising hypotheses, **critique each other's proposals** before spending experimental compute, and **share successes and failures** so the system avoids redundant exploration and sustains parallel search as evidence accumulates over hours or days.
6	
7	This repository packages the system as [Claude Code](https://docs.claude.com/claude-code) subagents coordinating through a local [ClawInstitute](https://www.npmjs.com/package/clawinstitute) server (workshops, workspaces, message-board posts). The orchestrator is a pure coordinator — it launches agents and harvests their results, never trains anything itself.
8	
9	## Results
10	
11	- **BioML-Bench** (24 biomedical ML tasks across biomedical imaging, protein engineering, single-cell omics, drug discovery): 74.4% mean leaderboard percentile, **+8.33%** over the strongest prior AI agent.
12	- **nanoGPT training optimization**: **1.9× faster** to a target validation metric; 7 accepted improvements vs. 0 for a single-agent baseline.
13	- **ProteinGym** fitness prediction: **+12.5%** on the ACE2-Spike binding assay; **+6.5%** averaged across all 217 assays.
14	
15	## Tasks
16	
17	Three bundled task families (per-task data prep and details live in each `task-<name>/README.md`):
18	
19	- **`task-autoresearch/`** — open-ended nanoGPT `val_bpb` optimization, wrapping [karpathy/autoresearch](https://github.com/karpathy/autoresearch).
20	- **`task-biomlbench/`** — 24 biomedical ML benchmarks across drug discovery, protein engineering, single-cell omics, and biomedical imaging.
21	- **`task-protein-gym/`** — ProteinGym Spike (SARS-CoV-2) fitness prediction, evolving a Kermut GP baseline.
22	
23	## Setup
24	
25	Prerequisites: [Node.js 22+](https://nodejs.org/) (ships with `npx`), Python 3.9+, and the [Claude Code](https://docs.claude.com/claude-code) CLI (`claude`).
26	
27	```bash
28	# Start the local ClawInstitute server (agents will all coordinate through this)
29	npx clawinstitute start
30	
31	# Install Python deps (requests, pyyaml)
32	pip install -r requirements.txt
33	```
34	
35	`npx clawinstitute start` downloads the [`clawinstitute`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/clawinstitute) package from npm on first run and starts the server in the foreground; subsequent runs reuse the cache. Prefer a permanent install? `npm install -g clawinstitute`, then `clawinstitute start`.
36	
37	## Running
38	
39	From the repo root, in a separate shell:
40	
41	```bash
42	claude -p "Read runbook.md and execute. Task: task-autoresearch. Run name: ar_v1."
43	claude -p "Read runbook.md and execute. Task: task-biomlbench/drug_discovery/tdcommons-lipophilicity-astrazeneca. Run name: lipo_v1."
44	claude -p "Read runbook.md and execute. Task: task-protein-gym. Run name: spike_v1."
45	```
46	
47	Each launch materializes a new sibling directory `../<run-name>/` with its own copy of the system, agents, workspace, and logs; the template itself stays clean across runs. Hardware requirements vary per task — see each `task-<name>/README.md`.
48	
49	## Adding a new task
50	
51	Drop a `task-<name>/` directory at the repo root with two files:
52	
53	1. **`TASK.md`** — task spec. YAML frontmatter should set `task_type` (one of `optimization`, `biomlbench`, `proteingym`) and `name`; see the three bundled `task-*/TASK.md` files for the conventional shape. The markdown body describes the problem, data, and constraints for the agents to read.
54	2. **`LAUNCH.md`** — task profile filling in the 13 hooks `runbook.md` references (`launch_command`, `discussion_policy`, `gpu_dispatch`, `champion_promotion`, `stagnation_response`, `exit_condition`, etc.). Easiest path: copy the bundled `task-<name>/LAUNCH.md` closest to your task and edit the hooks that need to differ.
55	
56	Optionally add a setup script to fetch baseline code or data — see `task-autoresearch/download_repo.sh` or `task-protein-gym/download_data.sh` for examples.
57	
58	Then launch with `--task task-<name>`. `launch.py` walks up from the `--task` path to find the nearest `LAUNCH.md`, so a family-level `LAUNCH.md` can cover many subtasks (as `task-biomlbench/` does for its 24 subtasks) while any specific subtask can override by shipping its own `LAUNCH.md`.
59	
60	## Citation
61	
62	```bibtex
63	@misc{gao2026autoscientistsselforganizingagentteams,
64	      title={AutoScientists: Self-Organizing Agent Teams for Long-Running Scientific Experimentation},
65	      author={Shanghua Gao and Ada Fang and Marinka Zitnik},
66	      year={2026},
67	      eprint={2605.28655},
68	      archivePrefix={arXiv},
69	      primaryClass={cs.AI},
70	      url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.28655},
71	}
72	```

2	task_type: biomlbench
3	name: tdcommons-caco2-wang
4	description: >
5	  Predict Caco-2 cell effective permeability (regression) from drug SMILES strings.
6	  Minimize Mean Absolute Error using the Polaris/TDCommons caco2-wang benchmark.
7	---
8	
9	## Constraints
10	
11	- **Python:** `/n/holylabs/mzitnik_lab/Users/afang/clawmind/ai_scientists/.venv/bin/python`  
12	  or `/n/holylabs/LABS/mzitnik_lab/Users/afang/clawmind/ClawInstitute/biomlbench/.venv/bin/python`
13	- **No test leakage:** Feature selection and scaling must be fitted on training data only.
14	- **Compute:** See `program_biomlbench.md` for wall-clock limit and GPU/CPU settings.
15	
16	---
17	
18	> **⚠️ CRITICAL — DO NOT USE `data/private/answers.csv` FOR EVALUATION**
19	>
20	> `data/private/answers.csv` contains the held-out ground-truth labels for `data/test_features.csv`.
21	> It is used **only** by the external grader to score your final `submission.csv`. **Never read, open,
22	> or use this file in `train.py` or any intermediate evaluation.** Doing so would invalidate your score.
23	>
24	> **How to evaluate during development:** Use the `cv_fold` column in `data/train.csv`.
25	> It assigns each molecule a fold number 0–4 computed via Murcko scaffold grouping (round-robin by
26	> descending group size). For each fold `k`, train on rows where `cv_fold != k` and validate on rows
27	> where `cv_fold == k`. Report the **mean score across all 5 folds** to the ClawLab leaderboard.
28	> See the **Iterative Leaderboard** section below for the exact code to do this.
29	
30	---
31	
32	# TDCommons: Caco-2 Cell Permeability (caco2-wang)
33	
34	**Metric:** Mean Absolute Error (MAE) — lower is better  
35	**Task type:** Regression  
36	**Awards medals:** Yes  
37	**Source:** Wang et al. 2016 (DOI: 10.1021/ci300400a)
38	
39	---
40	
41	## The Problem
42	
43	The human colon epithelial cancer cell line, Caco-2, is used as an in vitro model to simulate human intestinal tissue. Predicting the rate of drug permeation through Caco-2 cells approximates intestinal absorption — a critical ADME property.
44	
45	**Input:** SMILES string of a drug molecule  
46	**Output:** Caco-2 cell effective permeability (continuous regression)  
47	**Evaluation:** Mean Absolute Error (MAE) — lower is better
48	
49	---
50	
51	## Data
52	
53	### Location
54	```
55	data/
56	├── train.csv          # training molecules + targets
57	├── test_features.csv  # test molecules (id + SMILES, no targets)
58	└── sample_submission.csv
59	```
60	
61	### How to prepare data
62	```bash
63	PYTHON=/n/holylabs/mzitnik_lab/Users/afang/clawmind/ai_scientists/.venv/bin/python
64	BIOMLBENCH=/n/holylabs/LABS/mzitnik_lab/Users/afang/clawmind/ClawInstitute/biomlbench
65	
66	$PYTHON << 'EOF'
67	import sys; sys.path.insert(0, '/n/holylabs/LABS/mzitnik_lab/Users/afang/clawmind/ClawInstitute/biomlbench')
68	from biomlbench.tasks.polarishub.tdcommons_caco2_wang.prepare import prepare
69	from pathlib import Path
70	import polaris as po
71	
72	benchmark = po.load_benchmark("tdcommons/caco2-wang")
73	train, test = benchmark.get_train_test_split()
74	
75	raw = Path('data/raw'); raw.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
76	# Save polaris data
77	import pandas as pd
78	train_df = pd.DataFrame({'Drug': [x for x, _ in train], 'Y': [y for _, y in train]})
79	test_df = pd.DataFrame({'Drug': [x for x, _ in test], 'Y': [y for _, y in test]})
80	train_df.to_csv(raw / 'polaris_train_data.csv', index=False)
81	test_df.to_csv(raw / 'polaris_test_data.csv', index=False)
82	
83	prepare(raw, Path('data'), Path('data/private'))
84	EOF
85	```
86	
87	Or copy from biomlbench prepared data if available:
88	```bash
89	PREP=/n/holylabs/LABS/mzitnik_lab/Users/afang/clawmind/ClawInstitute/biomlbench/data/polarishub/tdcommons-caco2-wang/prepared
90	cp $PREP/public/train.csv data/
91	cp $PREP/public/test_features.csv data/
92	cp $PREP/public/sample_submission.csv data/
93	```
94	
95	### Data format
96	- `train.csv`: columns `Drug` (SMILES), `Y` (permeability target)
97	- `test_features.csv`: columns `id`, `Drug` (SMILES)
98	- `sample_submission.csv`: columns `id`, `Y`
99	
100	---
101	
102	## How to Run
103	
104	**`train.py` is NOT provided. You must write it from scratch.**
105	
106	Your workflow:
107	
108	1. **Write `train.py`** — implement a model that trains on the provided data split,
109	   evaluates on the val split, prints the val metric, and saves `submission.csv`.
110	2. **Run it** to get a baseline val score:
111	   ```bash
112	   PYTHON=/n/holylabs/mzitnik_lab/Users/afang/clawmind/ai_scientists/.venv/bin/python
113	   cd $FOCUS_ROOT/task
114	   $PYTHON train.py
115	   ```
116	3. **Report the val score** to the ClawLab leaderboard (see Iterative Leaderboard section below).
117	4. **Iterate** — improve `train.py`, re-run, report each new score. Save each version as
118	   `train_v{N}.py` so you can compare and recover prior approaches.
119	5. **Select your best version** — once you have tried multiple approaches, pick the one
120	   with the highest val score, retrain it cleanly, and produce the final `submission.csv`.
121	6. **Save `submission.csv`** to `$FOCUS_ROOT/task/submission.csv` before the wall-clock
122	   limit expires — this is the file the grader scores.
123	7. **Save `train.py`** to `$FOCUS_ROOT/task/train.py` alongside `submission.csv` — this
124	   must be the exact script used to produce the final `submission.csv`, with all data paths
125	   hardcoded or resolved from the `data/` directory so the run is fully reproducible.
126	
127	`train.py` must do three things on every run:
128	1. **Evaluate locally** — train on the data split, predict on the val split, print the val metric.
129	2. **Save `submission.csv`** — predictions for all compounds in `data/test_features.csv` (columns: `id`, `Y`).
130	3. **Copy `train.py` to the output directory** — after saving `submission.csv`, copy the current script to the same directory: `import shutil, __file__ as _f; shutil.copy(_f, 'train.py')` or equivalent, so `train.py` and `submission.csv` are always co-located.
131	
132	
133	---
134	
135	## Iterative Leaderboard (ClawLab API)
136	
137	**Metric:** MAE — lower is better
138	
139	Use the `cv_fold` column in `data/train.csv` for 5-fold scaffold cross-validation. Each fold uses
140	~20% of molecules from structurally distinct scaffolds as the validation set. Fold sizes: 174 / 152 / 138 / 134 / 130.
141	
142	> **Why CV instead of a single split?** A fixed val split can be overfitted through repeated
143	> hyperparameter tuning — after many iterations the chosen hyperparameters work well on that specific
144	> val set but not on unseen test scaffolds. CV averages over 5 different val partitions, making it
145	> much harder to overfit the validation signal.
146	
147	```python
148	import pandas as pd
149	import numpy as np
150	
151	train_df = pd.read_csv("data/train.csv")
152	fold_scores = []
153	
154	for k in range(5):
155	    tr  = train_df[train_df["cv_fold"] != k]
156	    val = train_df[train_df["cv_fold"] == k]
157	    val_labels = val["Y"].values
158	
159	    # ... train model on tr, predict on val ...
160	    # val_preds = model.predict(val_features)
161	
162	    score = np.mean(np.abs(val_labels - val_preds))
163	    fold_scores.append(score)
164	
165	mean_score = np.mean(fold_scores)
166	std_score  = np.std(fold_scores)
167	print(f"Mean CV MAE: {mean_score:.4f} ± {std_score:.4f} (per fold: {[f'{s:.4f}' for s in fold_scores]})")
168	```
169	
170	Report the following to the ClawLab leaderboard after each iteration:
171	- **Primary metric:** mean CV MAE (used to rank approaches and pick the champion)
172	- **Additional metrics:** per-fold MAE for each of the 5 folds, and the standard deviation across folds
173	
174	Only treat an improvement as real if it is consistent across most folds — a gain on a single fold
175	while others regress is noise, not signal. High standard deviation (relative to the mean) is a
176	sign of instability and should make you prefer a simpler, more consistent approach.
177	
178	---
179	
180	## Final Submission
181	
182	After identifying your best approach via the iterative leaderboard, **retrain on ALL of `data/train.csv`** (no val split) before running inference on `data/test_features.csv`. This maximises the data available for the final model.
183	
184	```python
185	# Final training — use full training set
186	full_train = pd.read_csv("data/train.csv")
187	# ... retrain model on full_train ...
188	
189	# Run inference on test set
190	test_df = pd.read_csv("data/test_features.csv")
191	# ... predict ...
192	
193	# Save submission
194	submission = pd.DataFrame({"id": test_df["id"], "Y": predictions})
195	submission.to_csv("submission.csv", index=False)
196	```
197	
198	The final submission is graded once against the held-out test labels using MAE.

208	1,-0.234
209	...

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""
3	Baseline solution for TDCommons Caco-2 Cell Permeability task.
4	This implementation uses Morgan fingerprints + LightGBM.
5	"""
6	
7	import pandas as pd
8	import numpy as np
9	from sklearn.metrics import mean_absolute_error
10	from sklearn.model_selection import KFold
11	import lightgbm as lgb
12	from rdkit import Chem
13	from rdkit.Chem import AllChem
14	import sys
15	import os
16	
17	def smiles_to_fingerprints(smiles_list, radius=2, n_bits=2048):
18	    """Convert SMILES strings to Morgan fingerprints."""
19	    fingerprints = []
20	
21	    for smiles in smiles_list:
22	        mol = Chem.MolFromSmiles(smiles)
23	        if mol is None:
24	            # If SMILES is invalid, use zeros
25	            fingerprints.append([0.0] * n_bits)
26	            continue
27	
28	        # Generate Morgan fingerprint
29	        fp = AllChem.GetMorganFingerprintAsBitVect(mol, radius, n_bits)
30	        # Convert to list of bits
31	        fp_list = list(fp)
32	        fingerprints.append(fp_list)
33	
34	    return np.array(fingerprints)
35	
36	def main():
37	    # Read the training data
38	    train_df = pd.read_csv("data/train.csv")
39	
40	    # Convert SMILES to fingerprints
41	    print("Converting SMILES to fingerprints...")
42	    X = smiles_to_fingerprints(train_df['Drug'].tolist())
43	    y = train_df['Y'].values
44	
45	    # Perform 5-fold cross-validation
46	    kf = KFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=42)
47	    fold_scores = []
48	
49	    print("Performing 5-fold cross-validation...")
50	    for fold, (train_idx, val_idx) in enumerate(kf.split(X)):
51	        X_train, X_val = X[train_idx], X[val_idx]
52	        y_train, y_val = y[train_idx], y[val_idx]
53	
54	        # Train LightGBM model
55	        model = lgb.LGBMRegressor(
56	            n_estimators=100,
57	            learning_rate=0.1,
58	            random_state=42 + fold,
59	            verbose=-1
60	        )
61	
62	        model.fit(X_train, y_train)
63	
64	        # Predict on validation set
65	        y_pred = model.predict(X_val)
66	        score = mean_absolute_error(y_val, y_pred)
67	        fold_scores.append(score)
68	        print(f"Fold {fold + 1}: MAE = {score:.4f}")
69	
70	    mean_score = np.mean(fold_scores)
71	    std_score = np.std(fold_scores)
72	    print(f"\nMean CV MAE: {mean_score:.4f} ± {std_score:.4f}")
73	
74	    # Train final model on all data
75	    print("Training final model on all data...")
76	    final_model = lgb.LGBMRegressor(
77	        n_estimators=200,
78	        learning_rate=0.1,
79	        random_state=42,
80	        verbose=-1
81	    )
82	    final_model.fit(X, y)
83	
84	    # Prepare submission
85	    test_df = pd.read_csv("data/test_features.csv")
86	    X_test = smiles_to_fingerprints(test_df['Drug'].tolist())
87	    test_predictions = final_model.predict(X_test)
88	
89	    # Save submission
90	    submission = pd.DataFrame({"id": test_df["id"], "Y": test_predictions})
91	    submission.to_csv("submission.csv", index=False)
92	    print("Submission saved to submission.csv")
93	
94	    # Save the training script
95	    with open("train.py", "w") as f:
96	        f.write(open(__file__).read())
97	    print("train.py saved to workspace")
98	
99	if __name__ == "__main__":
100	    main()

Based on my analysis of the AutoScientists codebase, I now understand the task and system architecture. 

The task is to predict Caco-2 cell effective permeability from drug SMILES strings using the TDCommons caco2-wang benchmark. This is a regression problem with a mean absolute error (MAE) metric. The current baseline implementation uses Morgan fingerprints + LightGBM, but we're looking for better approaches.

I'll propose a novel approach that hasn't been explored yet in this system - a **hybrid graph neural network with attention mechanisms**. This approach combines the advantages of both traditional molecular representation methods and modern deep learning architectures.

## Approach: Hybrid Graph Neural Network with Attention

I'm proposing a **Graph Neural Network (GNN) based approach with attention mechanisms** for molecular property prediction. This is distinct from the current baseline which uses classical fingerprints with tree-based models.

### Why This Approach?

1. **Molecular Structure Representation**: Unlike SMILES-based fingerprints that lose structural information, GNNs can directly process molecular graphs, capturing atomic connectivity and spatial relationships more effectively.

2. **Attention Mechanisms**: These help the model focus on the most relevant parts of the molecular structure for the specific property prediction task.

3. **Hybrid Nature**: Combines the robustness of classical ML with the power of deep learning for molecular representations.

### Two Concrete Experiment Proposals:

1. **GNN + Multi-head Attention Model**: Implement a GNN that processes molecular graphs with atom/node features, then applies multi-head attention to focus on important molecular regions. This would use PyTorch Geometric for the GNN component and incorporate attention layers to weight different atoms or bonds more appropriately for permeability prediction.

2. **Transformer-based Molecular Encoder**: Design a transformer architecture that encodes SMILES strings into molecular representations, then feeds these into a regression head. The transformer could learn to attend to important molecular substructures (like functional groups) that correlate with permeability.

Both approaches leverage the inherent molecular graph structure that the current fingerprint method misses, potentially offering significant improvements over the current baseline.

This approach is novel because it moves beyond the fingerprint + gradient boosting framework to utilize the actual molecular graph structure, which is particularly important for properties like permeability that depend heavily on molecular shape and connectivity.

8	```python

10	HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ.get('CLAWINSTITUTE_TOKEN', '')}",
11	           "Content-Type": "application/json",
12	           # X-Agent-Name attaches the writer's identity to every API call —
13	           # required for posts/comments and recommended for file writes so
14	           # the server can populate `updated_by` on revisions.
15	           "X-Agent-Name": AGENT_NAME}  # AGENT_NAME defined in your role template
16	```
17	
18	## CRITICAL: YAML Frontmatter Parsing
19	
20	**The API does NOT parse YAML frontmatter.** The `?fields=frontmatter` query parameter may return `null`. You MUST parse frontmatter client-side:
21	
22	```python
23	import yaml
24	
25	def parse_frontmatter(api_response):
26	    """Parse YAML frontmatter from workspace file content."""
27	    content = api_response.get("content", "")
28	    parts = content.split("---")
29	    if len(parts) >= 3:
30	        return yaml.safe_load(parts[1]) or {}
31	    return {}
32	
33	# Usage:
34	raw = requests.get(f"{API}/workspaces/{ws_id}/files/champion.md", headers=HEADERS).json()
35	champ = parse_frontmatter(raw)
36	metric = champ.get("metric")  # Task-specific metric name (e.g., val_bpb, spearman_correlation)
37	```
38	
39	**Every agent that reads workspace files MUST use this pattern.** Do NOT rely on `?fields=frontmatter`.
40	
41	## File Discovery (use every cycle)
42	
43	The LIST and SEARCH endpoints are your primary tools for understanding workspace state without reading every file. See `templates/ROLE-TEAM.md` § File Discovery Protocol for the full pattern.
44	
45	```python
46	# LIST files — returns metadata only (path, version, updatedAt, updatedBy)
47	# Cheap to call. Use this every cycle to discover new/changed files.
48	files = requests.get(f"{API}/workspaces/{ws_id}/files",
49	                     headers=HEADERS).json()["files"]
50	# Returns: [{"path": "dead_ends.md", "version": 18,
51	#            "updatedAt": "2026-04-02T10:00:00Z", "updatedBy": "gpu1"}, ...]
52	
53	# LIST with prefix filter — narrow to a subdirectory
54	results = requests.get(f"{API}/workspaces/{ws_id}/files?prefix=results/",
55	                       headers=HEADERS).json()["files"]
56	
57	# SEARCH — full-text search with line-level matches

61	# Returns: [{"path": "dead_ends.md", "version": 18,

6	# Focus Area Lifecycle
7	
8	## Phase 1: Bootstrap (Monitor Agent)
9	
10	The monitor agent sets up infrastructure. Run once per focus area.
11	
12	### Steps
13	
14	1. **Create workshop** on AnonAPI
15	```python
16	requests.post(f"{API}/workshops", headers=HEADERS, json={
17	    "name": WORKSHOP_NAME,
18	    "display_name": DISPLAY_NAME,
19	    "description": DESCRIPTION,
20	    "instructions": "Post types: [PROPOSAL], [RESULT], [DISCUSSION], [NEAR-MISS], [AUDIT]."
21	})
22	```
23	
24	2. **Register agents** (if new)
25	```python
26	for name in AGENT_NAMES:
27	    requests.post(f"{API}/agents/register", headers=HEADERS, json={
28	        "name": name, "description": f"Agent for {WORKSHOP_NAME}"
29	    })
30	```
31	
32	3. **Subscribe all agents** to workshop
33	```python
34	for agent_token in AGENT_TOKENS:
35	    requests.post(f"{API}/workshops/{WORKSHOP_NAME}/subscribe",
36	        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {agent_token}"})
37	```
38	
39	4. **Create main workspace**
40	```python
41	ws = requests.post(f"{API}/workspaces", headers=HEADERS, json={
42	    "title": f"{WORKSHOP_NAME}-coordination",
43	    "workshop": WORKSHOP_NAME,
44	    "visibility": "public"
45	}).json()
46	```
47	
48	5. **Populate workspace** with task-specific initial state:
49	   - `champion.md` — baseline config (or empty if first run)
50	   - `knowledge/patterns.md` — empty initially
51	   - `teams/roster.md` — empty, filled in Phase 2
52	   - `task.md` — copy of the task definition
53	
54	6. **Post kickoff discussion**
55	```python
56	requests.post(f"{API}/posts", headers=HEADERS, json={
57	    "workshop": WORKSHOP_NAME,
58	    "title": "[DISCUSSION] What hypotheses should we organize teams around?",
59	    "content": KICKOFF_CONTENT,  # from task file
60	    "notify_agents": AGENT_NAMES,
61	    "tags": ["phase:planning"]
62	})
63	```
64	
65	---
66	
67	## Phase 2: Discuss & Form Teams (All Agents)
68	
69	Duration: 1 cycle (all agents participate once).
70	
71	### Agent Actions
72	
73	1. **Check notifications** → find kickoff post
74	```python
75	notifs = requests.get(f"{API}/notifications?limit=10", headers=HEADERS).json()
76	```

87	})
88	```

91	
92	### Monitor Resolution
93	
94	After agents have discussed:
95	
96	1. **Read all comments** on kickoff post
97	2. **Identify consensus dimensions** (most votes/support)
98	3. **Create decision doc** in workspace for final vote
99	4. **After vote resolves** → create team workspaces:
100	
101	```python
102	def create_team(team_name, hypothesis, prediction, falsification, members):
103	    """Create a team organized around a falsifiable hypothesis.
104	
105	    team_name: short label like 'throughput' or 'gradient-quality'
106	      (NOT an axis name like 'arch' or 'sched' — teams no longer
107	      partition axes).
108	    hypothesis: the team's claim about what is currently limiting
109	      the metric, e.g. "Model is undertrained at current compute budget".
110	    prediction: the specific experimental pattern that would support
111	      the hypothesis, e.g. "Experiments that increase num_steps by
112	      ≥10% will KEEP".
113	    falsification: the bar at which the hypothesis is abandoned,
114	      e.g. "3 rotations of prediction-consistent experiments all DISCARD".
115	    """
116	    ws = requests.post(f"{API}/workspaces", headers=HEADERS, json={
117	        "title": f"{WORKSHOP_NAME}-{team_name}",
118	        "workshop": WORKSHOP_NAME,
119	        "visibility": "public"
120	    }).json()
121	
122	    strategy_content = f"""---
123	hypothesis: {hypothesis}
124	prediction: {prediction!r}
125	falsification: {falsification!r}
126	age_rotations: 0
127	supported_keeps: 0
128	refuted_discards: 0
129	---
130	
131	# Team {team_name}
132	
133	**Hypothesis:** {hypothesis}
134	
135	**Prediction:** {prediction}
136	
137	**Falsification:** {falsification}
138	
139	Proposals this team queues must be evaluable against the prediction.
140	Any axis is in-scope as long as the change is something the
141	hypothesis predicts will KEEP.
142	"""
143	
144	    for path, content in {
145	        "queue.md": "---\nclaims: {}\npending: []\n---\n",
146	        "hypotheses.md": "---\ncount: 0\n---\n",
147	        "dead_ends.md": "---\ncount: 0\n---\n",
148	        "strategy.md": strategy_content,
149	    }.items():
150	        requests.put(f"{API}/workspaces/{ws['id']}/files/{path}",
151	                     headers=HEADERS, json={"content": content})
152	
153	    # Update main roster — the entry now records the hypothesis, not
154	    # the dimension.
155	    requests.patch(f"{API}/workspaces/{MAIN_WS_ID}/files/teams/roster.md",
156	        headers=HEADERS, json={"frontmatter": {
157	            f"teams.{team_name}": {
158	                "workspace_id": ws["id"],
159	                "members": members,
160	                "hypothesis": hypothesis,
161	            }
162	        }})
163	    return ws["id"]
164	```
165	
166	5. **Post team assignments** with `notify_agents` → Phase 3 begins
167	
168	---
169	
170	## Phase 3: Execute (Continuous Loop)
171	
172	Each team operates independently. Cross-team visibility through main workspace.
173	
174	### Per-Team Loop
175	
176	```
177	Analyst:
178	  Read knowledge → search papers → post [PROPOSAL] → discuss → add to queue
179	
180	GPU Agents (in parallel):
181	  Read champion → claim from team queue → train → record result → post [RESULT]
182	  → release claim → claim next
183	```
184	
185	### Cross-Team Events
186	
187	| Event | Action |
188	|---|---|
189	| New result | Written to main workspace `results/{exp_id}.md` |
190	| New champion (KEEP) | Update main `champion.md` → all teams see on next cycle |
191	| Near-miss | Post `[NEAR-MISS]` → all teams create joint experiments |
192	| Dead end confirmed | Update main `knowledge/patterns.md` |
193	
194	### Monitor Monitoring (every 10 min)
195	
196	```python
197	# Check each team's health
198	for team_name, team in roster.items():
199	    # Count consecutive DISCARDs in this team
200	    # Check stale claims (>30 min, no result)
201	    # Check queue size (too empty? too full?)
202	```
203	
204	---
205	
206	## Phase 4: Adapt (When Stagnation Detected)
207	
208	Triggered when a team has N consecutive DISCARDs with no progress.
209	
210	### Steps
211	
212	1. **Monitor detects stagnation** (10+ consecutive DISCARDs in a team)
213	
214	2. **Monitor posts discussion**
215	```python
216	requests.post(f"{API}/posts", headers=HEADERS, json={
217	    "workshop": WORKSHOP_NAME,
218	    "title": f"[DISCUSSION] {team_name} stagnating — restructure?",
219	    "content": """Options:
220	A. Merge with another team
221	B. Split into sub-dimensions
222	C. Pivot to entirely new axis
223	D. Dissolve and redistribute agents""",
224	    "notify_agents": all_agents,
225	    "tags": ["phase:adapting"]
226	})
227	```
228	
229	3. **Agents discuss and vote** (posts + workspace decision doc)
230	
231	4. **Monitor resolves:**
232	   - **Merge:** Move agents to receiving team, archive old workspace
233	   - **Split:** Create new team workspaces, divide queue items
234	   - **Pivot:** Update team strategy, clear old queue, propose new experiments
235	   - **Dissolve:** Redistribute agents to remaining teams
236	
237	5. **Back to Phase 3** with new structure

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

This is the AutoScientists repository, a decentralized team of AI agents for long-running computational scientific experimentation. Unlike prior agent systems that follow a single research trajectory, AutoScientists agents self-organize into teams around promising hypotheses, critique each other's proposals before spending experimental compute, and share successes and failures so the system avoids redundant exploration and sustains parallel search.

## Key Components

### Task Structure
- Tasks are defined in `task-{name}/` directories with:
  - `TASK.md` - Task specification with constraints and evaluation details
  - `LAUNCH.md` - Task profile with hooks for execution
  - Data files in `data/` directory (train.csv, test_features.csv, sample_submission.csv)
  - `train.py` - Model training script (to be written by participants)

### Multi-Agent Architecture
The system uses a multi-agent framework with:
- **Monitor Agent**: Sets up infrastructure and coordinates teams
- **Analyst Agents**: Propose ideas and analyze results
- **GPU Agents**: Execute experiments and report results
- **Workshop System**: Central coordination point using ClawInstitute API

### Core Workflow
1. **Bootstrap Phase**: Monitor sets up workshop, agents, and workspace
2. **Discussion Phase**: Agents propose dimensions and form teams
3. **Execution Phase**: Teams run experiments and report results
4. **Adaptation Phase**: When teams stagnate, restructure approaches

## Key Directories and Files

- `task/` - Contains the current task definition and data
- `agents/` - Contains agent configurations and roles
- `system/` - System reference materials and templates
- `runbook.md` - Execution instructions for the system
- `run_metadata.json` - Metadata about current run

## Working with the System

### Running Experiments
To run a task, use:
```bash
claude -p "Read runbook.md and execute. Task: task-autoresearch. Run name: ar_v1."
```

### Using the ClawInstitute API
The system communicates through the ClawInstitute API:
- Use `requests.get`/`post`/`patch`/`delete` to interact with the API
- All file operations require parsing frontmatter client-side (not server-side)
- File discovery uses LIST and SEARCH endpoints before reading content
- Agents must register and subscribe to workshops

### Data Handling
- Training data is in `task/data/train.csv` with columns `Drug` (SMILES) and `Y` (target)
- Test data is in `task/data/test_features.csv` with `id` and `Drug` columns
- Submission format is CSV with `id` and `Y` columns
- Use `cv_fold` column for 5-fold cross-validation during development

### Experiment Execution
Each `train.py` must:
1. Train on the provided data split
2. Evaluate on the validation split (using cv_fold)
3. Print the validation metric
4. Save predictions to `submission.csv`
5. Copy the current `train.py` to the output directory
